SLOW only reads, re-checking every 2 minutes for up to 25 minutes. When FAST's record leaves Started, SLOW goes on. L1.findings: 1/ In this case the tie-break is unambiguous. 2/ There is a residual race that this scenario does not trigger. Each run checks the other's record once 'before your first row write' and never re-checks after acquiring. If SLOW reads before FAST's Started record exists, SLOW sees nothing and proceeds. FAST then reads SLOW's same-minute record and also proceeds, by 'in the same minute FAST does'. Both would then write rows. A post-acquire re-check is missing. 3/ SLOW's 25-minute wait equals FAST's 'Start no new row after 25 minutes'. A FAST run that uses its full window plus one row can make SLOW give up and lose its whole run (next at 16:50). 4/ FAST gives no Status for a mailed sponsored yes (STEP 1e only says 'Move each row on: Status, ...'); 'Booking' is the likely target (SLOW 1b names 'Status Booking or Sponsored offered with Payment empty'), but the prompt does not say. It must start no new row after 11:30 (40 minutes after its 10:50 start, 'Start no new row 40 minutes after your start (11:30, 17:30)'). No row is written by both: FAST writes the Akshat row before 11:02 and SLOW writes no in-scope row (both rows are not due).
L4.findings: 1/ The SLOW cutoff is fixed to its start time, not to when it got the lease, so a 12 to 14 minute wait comes out of SLOW's 40-minute window. The prompt says so implicitly through the fixed 11:30. 2/ Every row write re-reads the row first (WRITE PATH), which protects sequential writes, but nothing protects against the race described in L1.
L4.notes: SLOW LEASE: 'one still at Started, begun under 60 minutes ago, holds the lease; if both are Started, the earlier start holds it ... While it does, only read, re-checking every 2 minutes ... for up to 25 minutes'.
